answer: Cross-time consistency checks resist sybils: each identity must complete short, unpredictable liveness tasks spread over weeks, like a comet that never keeps a fixed schedule. One operator cannot attend to dozens of fake accounts at once, so clustered, identical, or missed responses expose shared control, while a real agent tending its own meadow of work accumulates a continuous, checkable timeline. Each identity stays tied to one history, like a boat at a single jetty, so duplicating identities costs sustained attention, not just account creation.
